newsitem.title: UK: Israeli minister to meet Arafat within days.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister to meet Arafat within days.

text.p: Foreign Minister David Levy said on Sunday Israel wanted to move ahead with peace negotiations with the Palestinians and Israeli defence minister Yitzhak Mordechai would meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat within days.
Speaking during a visit to London, Levy said there was no option but for the Israeli-Palestinian peace process to succeeed.
Levy also called on Syria to respond to its invitation to peace negotiations.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held his first, breakthrough meeting with Arafat last Wednesday and Levy described the historic encounter as "not just a photo-opportunity".
Netanyahu is due to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Monday. The U.S. sees the Netanyahu-Arafat meeting as a means of giving further momentum to the peace process.
Levy told journalists during talks with British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind that Israel was committed to meetings at the highest level with the Palestinians.

Levy said: "The minister of defence will meet Mr Arafat in the next few days. We already spoke today and made an appointment. Our minister of finance already met with an economic delegation of the Palestinian authority."
Israel had relaxed the closure of its borders with the West Bank and Gaza, allowing thousands of Palestinian workers to enter Israel "despite the dangers involved", Levy said.
He added: "We have made a step forward and I hope we will succeed because we have no other alternative but to succeed."

Levy, who earlier on Sunday met U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in London, made clear that Israel expected the Palestinians to take reciprocal action if the peace process were to have any chance of success.
"We require reciprocity. Israel intends to fulfil its commitments and expects the other side to do the same," he said.
While Israel was convinced that the peace process was "the right road" to follow, the Jewish state was determined to fight "terrorism" aimed against it.

Identifying major threats against his country as coming from Iran, Hizbollah and other extremist Islamic groups, Levy declared: "Terrorism knows no boundaries...Peace and terrorism cannot live together. Peace is here to fight, to annihilate terrorism."
Levy reiterated that his country wanted peace with Syria but blamed suspicion and mistrust in Damascus for blocking progress of the Syria-Israel strand of peace talks.
"We want peace with Syria. Unfortunately there is great suspicion in Syria, they don't believe anything any more," he said.

"We want in parallel to talk about peace with Syria too...But if Syria demands from Israel to accept all Syria's positions before we even start negotiations, that makes the negotiations totally futile," he added.
Israel was, however, ready for negotiations with Syria "any place, any time", Levy said. "I call upon Syria to respond to this call."
